answer: Arrival-curve gating treats identity creation as a traffic-shape problem: new agents must spread registrations across time slots, and burst joins get queued behind a jade delay that grows with cluster size. A single legitimate anchor agent can pre-clear its slot instantly, but a mass of fresh addresses cannot. Each extra identity costs the attacker real waiting time and forfeited parallel capacity, and any timing ripple from coordinated joins is flagged and throttled.
